bugs: Store and tag sync are not wrapped in a transaction, so if the tag sync fails the post still exists (PostController.php:31-32). impl-2 has the same issue.
syncTagNames runs one firstOrCreate per tag (Post.php:55). That is N+1 writes, and two requests adding the same new tag at once can hit the unique constraint.
antipatterns: app/Models/Post.php:52 calls trim() on each tag name, but the TrimStrings middleware already trims input, so this is redundant.
routes/api.php:6-11 lists the routes by hand instead of using apiResource()->except('show'). The ->can() middleware justifies it, but it is more code.
app/Http/Requests/StorePostRequest.php:17 sets no maximum number of tags.
strengths: Route-level ->can('update','post') middleware returns 403 before validation runs, and a test checks this (test_non_author_gets_403_before_validation).
The controller is thin: no auth calls, safe()->except('tags'), and posts are created through the user relation.
Uses #[Scope], #[Fillable] and #[ObservedBy] attributes, an enum cast, Rule::enum, and whenLoaded with pluck in the resource.
Tag sync is collection-based: it trims, drops empty names, de-duplicates, then syncs.
Tests use hasAttached factories, freezeSecond and assertModelMissing, and cover guests, 403, 404, validation, filters, pagination and cross-user tag leakage.

bugs: Gate::authorize runs inside the controller, after the FormRequest has validated. A non-author sending an invalid payload gets 422 with validation details instead of the required 403 (probe confirmed: PUT with title '' returned 422). See PostController.php:40.
Store and tag sync are not wrapped in a transaction (PostController.php:32-33).
antipatterns: app/Http/Controllers/PostController.php:40,50 call Gate::authorize in the controller, when route ->can() middleware or FormRequest authorize() would run before validation.
app/Models/Post.php:51-54 uses insertOrIgnore and sets timestamps by hand. This bypasses Eloquent, and on MySQL insertOrIgnore also hides errors unrelated to duplicates.
app/Models/Post.php:49 uses array_values(array_unique()) where a collection would read better. It is also redundant, because the 'distinct' rule already rejects duplicates.
tests/Feature/PostApiTest.php:235 uses the \DB facade alias without importing it.
The 'distinct' rule rejects duplicate tags with 422 rather than ignoring them, which is less forgiving for API clients.
strengths: Tag upsert is bulk: insertOrIgnore followed by a whereIn/pluck, so there are no per-tag queries.
Validation is tighter: tags capped at max:20 and 'distinct' on names.
request->whenHas('tags', ...) is a neat way to replace tags only when the field is sent.
Has a composite index on (user_id, status, created_at) that fits the index query.
Tests cover guests without an Accept header, an N+1 query budget, and query-string preservation in pagination links.

v.rationale:
I rank impl-1 first (8.6 overall) and impl-2 second (8.1). The two are nearly the same: same enum, observer for the slug and published_at, `#[Scope]`/`#[Fillable]`/`#[ObservedBy]` attributes, resource, and index scopes. Both test suites pass: impl-1 ran 30 tests, impl-2 ran 28.

**What decides it:** impl-2 checks authorization with `Gate::authorize` inside the controller, which runs after the FormRequest has validated. My probe showed a non-author sending invalid data gets 422 with error details, not 403. That breaks the "403 otherwise" requirement and leaks validation detail. impl-1 puts `->can()` middleware on the routes, so it returns 403 before validation, and a test pins this down.

**Where impl-2 is better:** its tag upsert is bulk (`insertOrIgnore`) and it validates more tightly (`max:20` tags, `distinct`). impl-1 instead calls `firstOrCreate` once per tag, and its `trim()` is redundant because the TrimStrings middleware already trims input.

**Shared gaps:** neither wraps the post create and tag sync in a transaction.

**Other probes:** null tags, a null tag in the list, an array passed as `tag`, and an empty `status` behaved the same in both (all 422). `GET /api/posts/{post}` returns 405 in both. Real authorization matters more than how tags are written, so impl-1 ranks first.
